result.notes: The Unified District Information System for Education (UDISE) is an initiative by the Government of India to collate and manage data related to the education sector at the school level. Launched under the aegis of the Ministry of Education, UDISE serves as a comprehensive database, capturing detailed information about school infrastructure, teacher qualifications, student enrollment, and other crucial educational parameters. The data is collected annually from pre-primary to higher secondary school levels across all Indian states and union territories. UDISE plays a pivotal role in assisting policymakers, educators, and researchers in understanding the state of education in India, enabling informed decision-making and the formulation of targeted interventions. The platform's insights and analytics contribute significantly to enhancing the quality and accessibility of education in the country.

resources.description: UDISE (Unified District Information System for Education) is a comprehensive database of the schools in India, which covers over 1.5 million schools, 9.6 million teachers, and 264 million children. It is a management information system that collects, collates, and disseminates data related to various aspects of school education.

resources.data_insights: Which states have the highest and lowest dropout rates at the secondary level, and how have they changed from 2018-19 to 2022-23? How do gross and net enrolment ratios fall from primary to higher secondary across states? Which states have the biggest gaps in functional toilets, drinking water, electricity and internet in government schools? How does the pupil-teacher ratio differ across states and school levels? How has enrolment of children with special needs changed over the years?
resources.description: State- and UT-level indicators on school education in India, compiled from the annual UDISE+ booklets published by the Ministry of Education for 2018-19 to 2022-23. They cover the number of schools and teachers (total, government and government-aided), pupil-teacher ratios, and enrolment by school management and level (pre-primary, primary, upper primary, secondary and higher secondary), including children with special needs. They also include gross, net, adjusted net and age-specific enrolment ratios, the gender parity index, and promotion, repetition, dropout, transition and retention rates. School facilities covered are electricity, drinking water, toilets, handwashing, library, medical check-ups, computers, internet, and ramps and handrails for children with special needs. Levels follow the grade structure (Classes 1–5, 6–8, 9–10 and 11–12)
resources.name: State-wise School Education Indicators (2018-19 to 2022-23)

resources.description: State- and UT-level indicators on school education in India, compiled from the annual UDISE+ booklets published by the Ministry of Education for 2023-24 to 2025-26. From 2023-24, UDISE+ reports by the stages of the National Education Policy 2020 (Foundational, Preparatory, Middle and Secondary) instead of grade bands. The indicators cover the number of schools and teachers, pupil-teacher ratios by stage, and enrolment by school management and stage, including children with special needs. They also include gross, net, adjusted net and age-specific enrolment ratios, the gender parity index, and dropout, transition and retention rates. School facilities covered are electricity, drinking water, toilets, handwashing, library, medical check-ups, computers, internet, and ramps and handrails for children with special needs
resources.name: State-wise School Education Indicators by NEP Stage 2023 Onwards
